segmentNote: Two businesses: engineering and construction (81% of revenue, 70% of profit) and property development (19% of revenue, 30% of profit). Malaysia and Australia are the two biggest markets (FS p.90-91).

balance.note: Borrowings rose to RM14.1bn to buy land in Vietnam and Singapore; net gearing reached 72%, just above Gamuda's own 70% limit. Management expects it to fall from next year as projects bring in cash (QR p.10; FS p.89).

cash.wfNote: Operations turned cash-positive (RM755m) in FY2026, but buying land in Vietnam and Singapore, Penang reclamation and joint-venture investments took RM3.4bn, funded mainly with RM4.1bn of new borrowing.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM27.2 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (FY2026)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM26 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (FY2026)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2026 dividends)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM2.2 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM57 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 2.1 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (FY2026)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM8 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin FY2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM5.71.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth FY2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Net debt
metrics.plain: Borrowings minus cash: RM9.43 billion owed to lenders after using all its cash.

metrics.label: Net gearing
metrics.plain: Net debt is 72% of shareholders' funds. Under 50% is usually seen as comfortable; above 100% means lenders fund more than owners.

metrics.label: Free cash flow FY2026
metrics.plain: Cash from operations minus spending on assets and land: RM-1,883 million. Negative means it borrowed or used savings to fund growth.

metrics.label: Free cash flow yield
metrics.plain: That spare cash as a share of the company's market value.

metrics.label: EV / EBITDA
metrics.plain: A price tag that includes debt: about 19.7 times its yearly cash earnings before interest and tax.

drivers.evidence: Construction orderbook at an all-time high of RM61bn after RM25.1bn of new wins in FY2026 (QR p.10)
drivers.why: Work already won gives years of revenue visibility; new wins are the main thing investors watch.

drivers.evidence: Hyperscale data centres at Eco Business Park V (RM2.1bn) and Port Dickson (RM1.7bn) won in FY2026 (QR p.10)
drivers.why: Management expects domestic data-centre builds to anchor next year's earnings (QR p.10).

drivers.evidence: RM7.3bn Stations Package West won in Australia, plus solar, wind and battery projects (QR p.10)
drivers.why: Australia is as big as Malaysia by revenue; large transport and energy jobs keep it growing.

drivers.evidence: RM2.2bn Kaohsiung MRT Xiaogang-Linyuan line won in the fourth quarter (QR p.10)
drivers.why: Taiwan revenue rose from RM0.7bn to RM1.2bn; more metro work adds a third growth market.

drivers.evidence: Property sales fell to RM3.2bn from RM4.1bn (IR p.62)
drivers.why: Lower sales today mean less property revenue to recognise in coming years.

drivers.evidence: Strong take-up at Eaton Park in Ho Chi Minh City; buyers pay half at handover by law (QR p.10)
drivers.why: Large profits and cash are expected when these projects are handed over.

drivers.evidence: RM7.6bn of property already sold but not yet recognised (QR p.10)
drivers.why: Future property revenue that is already locked in.

drivers.evidence: Net gearing rose to 72%, above the self-imposed 70% ceiling, after land purchases (QR p.10; FS p.89)
drivers.why: More debt means more interest cost; management expects gearing to fall from next year.

drivers.evidence: Operating cash flow of RM755m vs a small deficit in FY2025, mostly earned in the fourth quarter (FS p.13; QR p.10)
drivers.why: Shows profits are starting to turn into cash.

drivers.evidence: Skilled-labour shortages, wage pressure, subcontractor insolvencies and material price swings named as risks (IR p.34)
drivers.why: Fixed-price contracts can lose margin when costs rise.

drivers.evidence: 60% of revenue is earned outside Malaysia; borrowings of RM14.1bn (FS p.91, p.89)
drivers.why: Higher rates raise borrowing costs; currency moves change ringgit profit.

drivers.evidence: Net dividend of 10 sen per share, the same as FY2025 (FS p.10)
drivers.why: Steady payout while cash goes into growth.

drivers.evidence: About 26 times FY2026 profit at RM4.56 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: A growth premium; slower contract wins could weigh on the share price.

outlook.text: Next year's earnings expected to be anchored by domestic construction, including hyperscale data centres, plus higher profit from property projects in Vietnam and Singapore (QR p.10).
Earnings visibility underpinned by a record RM61bn construction orderbook and RM7.6bn of unbilled property sales (QR p.10).
Net gearing of 72% is temporarily above the 70% limit; expected to come down from next year as projects generate cash (QR p.10).
Risks named: skilled-labour shortages, wage and material costs, subcontractor insolvency and supply-chain bottlenecks (IR p.34).

outlookOverall.text: Management expects next year to be anchored by its record orderbook and property launches (QR p.10).
